A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Looped Transformers for Length Generalization, with matching authors, framework, tasks, and appendix programs. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-task length-generalization experiments, ablations, stopping analyses, and measured inference times in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and reports additional comparisons of oracle, whole-test-set, per-sample, and fixed-depth stopping in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The recurrent decoder-only architecture, input injection, NoPE, final-output loss, and step-supervised training are retained. FAP becomes FOP. The corrected argmin agrees with v1's minimum-loss description, while batch notation clarifies stopping aggregation; these do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Parity, repeated-token Copy, Binary Addition, Binary Sum, Binary Multiplication, and Unique Set with the same task requirements. Revised length ranges and stopping procedures remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds FOP-Loop-Fixed, a fixed-depth full-output comparator distinct from the retained NTP-Loop baseline. Other NTP and FAP/FOP comparators remain. UT and PonderNet appear in a descriptive architectural table, not a new empirical benchmark.

E3.justification: Reported configurations change materially: Parity uses 64 rather than 8 heads; Binary Sum uses 16 rather than 8 heads and 2 rather than 3 block layers. Both curriculum intervals change from 1000 to 500 updates. Parity's stated training interval changes from [1,20) to [1,20], while plotted test maxima contract from 50 to 40 for Parity and 30 to 24 for Binary Sum. v3 also adds per-sample versus whole-test-set stopping and a fixed-depth control. Updated curves therefore cannot be treated as same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix C adds a six-task comparison testing the effects of oracle, whole-test-set confidence, per-sample confidence, and fixed-depth stopping. Existing input-injection and pause-token ablations remain, with revised Parity/Binary Sum panels. Most additional stepwise traces from v1 Appendix C disappear; its 40-digit Parity trace moves into the main text.

E5.justification: Both experimental-details appendices report mean exact-match accuracy and standard errors from five training runs with different random seeds. v3 retains this practice rather than introducing additional runs or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Parity and Binary Sum curves are replaced under revised settings, and v1's report of Parity accuracy above 0.95 at 100 digits is removed. New Figure 7 shows approximately chance-level per-sample stopping on Parity and very low accuracy on Binary Sum despite strong oracle/batch results. The measured inference-time table, including 0.1967 seconds for oracle stopping and 0.2190 seconds for confidence stopping, is also removed.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 explicitly adds preprocessing/postprocessing stages and requires these and the repeated step to belong to RASP-L; v1 already used such stages in its examples and footnote. Equation 2 corrects argmax to argmin of cross-entropy. The three propositions, appendix programs, and asymptotic complexity analysis otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and concluding claim retain the same central assertions: define n-RASP-L, train looped Transformers using final-answer and step-count supervision, and improve length generalization through adaptive depth.

C2.justification: v1 describes confidence stopping as selecting near-perfect accuracy without distinguishing aggregation. v3 explains that per-sample stopping works substantially worse on non-converging Parity and Binary Sum, connecting reliability to convergence. Section 7 also newly states that the current n-RASP-L definition excludes tasks requiring multiple sequential loops. These materially qualify applicability.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents EMA with factor 0.9999 for Parity/Binary Sum and specifies the fixed-depth FOP comparator's depth. Table 2 provides task-specific head counts and revised hyperparameters. Conversely, v1's disclosure of 4–6 hours per run on an NVIDIA A100 40 GB is removed. Code access and most implementation information remain.

R1.justification: Section 5 expands the Universal Transformer/PonderNet comparison into Table 1, emphasizes claimed FOP and step-supervision innovations, and adds Bolukbasi et al. (2017). The remaining research positioning and cited works are largely retained.

P1.justification: Full-answer prediction/FAP becomes full-output prediction/FOP throughout. There are localized prose revisions, expanded stopping and related-work explanations, reorganized appendices, and subdivided experimental details. The main narrative and section order remain, alongside ICLR headers, author-year citations, and new acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v3 adds an architectural comparison table and a six-panel stopping comparison, removes the timing table and most supplementary stopping traces, and relocates the main ablation figure to Appendix B. The hyperparameter table gains a head-count column, and Parity/Binary Sum plot axes and captions change. These substantially revise the evidence displays beyond template changes and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 makes adaptive-inference evidence more informative by adding a fixed-depth control, exposing per-sample stopping failures, clarifying aggregation, and correcting the loss-minimization equation. Explicit applicability limits also improve interpretation. These gains modestly outweigh the narrower reported length tests and removal of useful runtime and hardware information.
